title: Inviting, asking and wanting
title_target: いっしょに いきませんか — Issho ni ikimasen ka
goal: Invite people, say what you want and want to do, ask for permission, and turn things down without giving offense.
bekal: inviting with ～ませんか and ～ましょう
expressing wishes with ～たいです and ～が ほしいです
asking permission with ～てもいいですか

dialogs.title: 会話 1 — A weekend invitation
dialogs.intro: Tanaka invites Ani out. Notice that invitations in Japanese take the form of a negative question — and that's exactly what makes them polite.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [アニさん|Ani-san]、[こんどの|kondo no] [どようび|doyōbi]、[ひまですか|hima desu ka]。
lines.id: Ani, are you free this Saturday?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[ひまです|hima desu]。
lines.id: Yes, I'm free.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [いっしょに|Issho ni] [おまつりへ|omatsuri e] [いきませんか|ikimasen ka]。
lines.id: Would you like to go to the festival together?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [いいですね|Ii desu ne]！[わたしも|Watashi mo] [おまつりが|omatsuri ga] [みたいです|mitai desu]。
lines.id: Sounds great! I'd like to see a festival too.
lines.literal: good — is — right! I — also — festival — [subject] — want-to-see — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [じゃあ|Jā]、[なんじに|nanji ni] [あいましょうか|aimashō ka]。
lines.id: So, what time shall we meet?

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [ろくじは|Roku-ji wa] [どうですか|dō desu ka]。
lines.id: How about six?

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [いいですよ|Ii desu yo]。[えきの|Eki no] [まえで|mae de] [あいましょう|aimashō]。
lines.id: Sure. Let's meet in front of the station.
lines.literal: good — is — you-know. station — 's — front — at — let's-meet.

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [おまつりで|Omatsuri de] [なにが|nani ga] [たべられますか|taberaremasu ka]。
lines.id: What can you eat at the festival?

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [たこやきや|Takoyaki ya] [やきそばが|yakisoba ga] [あります|arimasu]。[たこやきを|Takoyaki o] [たべたいですか|tabetai desu ka]。
lines.id: There's takoyaki, yakisoba and so on. Do you want to try takoyaki?
lines.literal: takoyaki — and-such — yakisoba — [subject] — exist. takoyaki — [object] — want-to-eat — [question].

lines.speaker: アニ:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[たべたいです|tabetai desu]！[ゆかたも|Yukata mo] [きたいです|kitai desu]。
lines.id: Yes, I want to! I'd like to wear a yukata too.
lines.literal: yes, want-to-eat — is! yukata — also — want-to-wear — is.

lines.speaker: たなか:
lines.text: [じゃあ|Jā]、[ごじに|go-ji ni] [きてください|kite kudasai]。[ははが|Haha ga] [てつだいます|tetsudaimasu]。
lines.id: Then come at five. My mother will help you.
lines.literal: well-then, five-o'clock — at — come-please. mother — [subject] — helps.

notes: **Inviting with a negative sounds more polite.** いきませんか (“won't you go?”) leaves the door open to say no, while いきましょう (“let's go”) already assumes a yes. That's why the first invitation almost always uses ～ませんか; ～ましょう comes later, once the person has agreed.
**Notice the flow in this dialogue:** Tanaka invites with いきませんか → Ani agrees → only then does あいましょう appear. This order is no accident, and following it makes your conversations sound natural.
**～ましょうか = “shall we ～?”** — offering while asking. なんじに あいましょうか = what time shall we meet? Also used to offer help: てつだいましょうか (shall I help?).
**や = “and so on”**, unlike と, which gives a complete list. たこやき**と**やきそば = takoyaki and yakisoba (that's all). たこやき**や**やきそば = takoyaki, yakisoba, and other things.

**きます has two different meanings:** 来ます (come) and 着ます (wear clothes). In this dialogue きたいです = want to **wear**, not want to come. Different kanji, same kana — one of the reasons kanji are still used.
**Yukata** (ゆかた) is a light cotton kimono worn at summer festivals. Unlike formal kimono, it's cheaper, simpler, and young people love wearing it.

grammars.title: Inviting: four levels
body: All are formed from the [ます|masu] form by changing the ending. What differs is how much room you leave for a no.
after: Accepting — **[いいですね|ii desu ne]。** (Sounds good.) / **[ぜひ|zehi]。** (I'd love to.) / **[いきましょう|ikimashō]。** (Let's go.)

Declining — **[すみません|sumimasen]、[ちょっと|chotto]…** (Sorry, it's a bit…) / **[その日は|sono hi wa] [ちょっと|chotto]…** (That day's a bit…). ⚠️ Answering [いいえ|iie]、[いきません|ikimasen] sounds very cold and is almost never used.

grammars.title: ～[たいです|tai desu] — want to do
body: To say you **want to do something**, drop [ます|masu] and add **[たい|tai]**. The result behaves like an [い|i]-adjective — so its negative and past follow the rules from Unit 7.

head: Form
Example
Meaning
rows: [たべます|tabemasu] → [たべたいです|tabetai desu]
[いきます|ikimasu] → [いきたいです|ikitai desu]
[かいます|kaimasu] → [かいたいです|kaitai desu]

after: **The object can take [を|o] or [が|ga].** [すしを|sushi o] [たべたいです|tabetai desu] and [すしが|sushi ga] [たべたいです|tabetai desu] are both correct; the [が|ga] version puts slightly more stress on the thing.

⚠️ **Don't use ～[たいです|tai desu] for a third person.** Japanese assumes you can't know what's in someone else's heart, so “he wants to go” needs another form ([いきたがっています|ikitagatte imasu]). Use ～[たいです|tai desu] only for yourself and when asking the person you're talking to.
**Its relative: ～[が|ga] [ほしいです|hoshii desu]** = want to **have** (a thing). [あたらしいくるまが|atarashii kuruma ga] [ほしいです|hoshii desu] = I want a new car. Use [ほしい|hoshii] for things, [たい|tai] for actions.

dialogs.title: 会話 2 — Asking permission in class
dialogs.intro: Budi asks his teacher for a few things. Notice how the patterns for permission and prohibition come in pairs.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [せんせい|Sensei]、[しつもんが|shitsumon ga] [あります|arimasu]。
lines.id: Sensei, I have a question.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[どうぞ|dōzo]。
lines.id: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [すみません|Sumimasen]、[この|kono] [ことばの|kotoba no] [いみが|imi ga] [わかりません|wakarimasen]。
lines.id: Excuse me, I don't understand what this word means.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [じしょで|Jisho de] [しらべてください|shirabete kudasai]。
lines.id: Look it up in the dictionary.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [スマホを|Sumaho o] [つかっても|tsukatte mo] [いいですか|ii desu ka]。
lines.id: May I use my phone?

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [はい|Hai]、[いいですよ|ii desu yo]。でも、[じゅぎょうちゅうは|jugyōchū wa] [でんわは|denwa wa] [だめです|dame desu]。
lines.id: Yes, that's fine. But no phone calls during class.
lines.literal: yes, good — is — you-know. but, class-during — as-for — phone-call — as-for — no-good — is.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [わかりました|Wakarimashita]。[あと|Ato]、[すこし|sukoshi] [はやく|hayaku] [かえっても|kaette mo] [いいですか|ii desu ka]。
lines.id: Understood. Also, may I leave a little early?
lines.literal: understood. also, a-little — early — go-home — even-if — good — is — [question].

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [どうしてですか|Dōshite desu ka]。
lines.id: Why?

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [びょういんへ|Byōin e] [いきますから|ikimasu kara]。
lines.id: Because I'm going to the hospital.

lines.speaker: せんせい:
lines.text: [そうですか|Sō desu ka]。[じゃあ|Jā]、[だいじょうぶです|daijōbu desu]。[おだいじに|Odaiji ni]。
lines.id: I see. In that case, it's fine. Take care of yourself.
lines.literal: so — is — [question]. well-then, all-right — is. honorable-important — to.

lines.speaker: ブディ:
lines.text: [ありがとうございます|Arigatō gozaimasu]。[しつれいします|Shitsurei shimasu]。
lines.id: Thank you. Excuse me.

notes: **～てもいいですか = “may I ～?”.** Literally “even if I ～, is it good?”. This is the most common permission pattern and you'll need it constantly: ここに すわってもいいですか (may I sit here?), しゃしんを とってもいいですか (may I take a photo?).
**だめです = not allowed.** Short and firm. A softer version: **ちょっと…** — yet another trailing-off sentence.

**から at the end of a sentence = because.** びょういんへ いきます**から** = because I'm going to the hospital. Note the position: in a full sentence the reason comes first and the result second — the reverse of English, where “because” usually comes second.
**どうして / なぜ = why.** どうして is more common in conversation, なぜ more written. The answer ends in から.
**おだいじに = take care / get well soon.** A set phrase for someone who's ill or on the way to the doctor. You'll hear it from pharmacists and doctors every time.
**じゅぎょうちゅう = during class.** The suffix ～ちゅう (中) means “in progress”: しごとちゅう (at work), でんわちゅう (on the phone), こうじちゅう (under construction).

grammars.title: Permission, prohibition and requests
body: All three are built from the **[て|te]-form** — the most versatile verb form in Japanese. How to make it is fully explained in Unit 10; here you'll use it as a ready-made package first.

head: Pattern
Example
Meaning
rows: [すわっても|Suwatte mo] [いいですか|ii desu ka]。
[かえっても|Kaette mo] [いいです|ii desu]。
[ここで|Koko de] [たべては|tabete wa] [いけません|ikemasen]。
[でんわは|Denwa wa] [だめです|dame desu]。
[しゃしんを|Shashin o] [とらないで|toranaide] [ください|kudasai]。

after: **The ten most useful [て|te]-forms — learn them as whole words:** [きて|kite] (come), [みて|mite] (look), [まって|matte] (wait), [いって|itte] (say/go), [かいて|kaite] (write), [よんで|yonde] (read), [たべて|tabete] (eat), [のんで|nonde] (drink), [して|shite] (do), [すわって|suwatte] (sit).

grammars.title: Declining without saying no
body: This is the part of the culture that most often trips up foreigners. Japanese has a whole range of very gentle refusals, and native speakers read the signals easily.

head: Sentence
What it really means
rows: [その日は|Sono hi wa] [ちょっと|chotto]…
I'll think about it — usually means no.
[むずかしいですね|Muzukashii desu ne]。
That's difficult — almost always means no.

after: ⚠️ **Don't push after hearing [ちょっと|chotto].** Repeating an invitation after a gentle refusal is seen as pressuring. The right response: **[そうですか|sō desu ka]、[ざんねんです|zannen desu]。[またこんど|mata kondo]。** (I see, that's a shame. Next time, then.)
**It works both ways.** If you want to decline, [ちょっと|chotto] is enough — you don't need to build a long excuse. In fact, Japanese people won't ask any further.

blocks.text: The most basic reason pattern: **[reason] から、[result]。** The reason comes first. In conversation it can also be flipped, with から at the end of the sentence as a short answer.

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: [あついですから|Atsui desu kara]、[まどを|mado o] [あけます|akemasu]。
It's hot, so I'll open the window.
[じかんが|Jikan ga] [ありませんから|arimasen kara]、[いきません|ikimasen]。
I don't have time, so I won't go.
[どうして|Dōshite] [きませんでしたか|kimasen deshita ka]。 — [びょうきでしたから|Byōki deshita kara]。
Why didn't you come? — Because I was sick.
[やすいですから|Yasui desu kara]、[かいます|kaimasu]。
It's cheap, so I'll buy it.

blocks.title: から and ので
items: **から** = because, fairly direct. Good for personal reasons and ordinary conversation.
**ので** = because, softer and less defensive-sounding. Used when asking permission or explaining to a superior: **[びょういんへ|byōin e] [いきますので|ikimasu node]**…
At A1, から is enough. Just recognize ので so it doesn't confuse you when you hear it.

blocks.text: If you could memorize only ten sentences from this whole module, make it these ten. You've met them all, and every one is useful from your first day in Japan.

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: [ありがとうございます|Arigatō gozaimasu]。
[もういちど|Mō ichido] [おねがいします|onegaishimasu]。
[にほんごが|Nihongo ga] [すこし|sukoshi] [わかります|wakarimasu]。
[えいごが|Eigo ga] [はなせますか|hanasemasu ka]。

blocks.text: Copy these ten sentences into your phone. Not to read when you need them — you won't have time — but to reread five times a day until they come out without thinking.
